vision: The college is guided by the visionary zeal of providing value-based education to everyone irrespective of religion, caste, creed or sex by which the character is formed.
mission: At St. Philomena’s College, our mission is to holistically transform young men and women into intellectually curious, emotionally resilient, and socially responsible individuals. By fostering a dynamic learning environment where students live, learn, work, and play together, we nurture essential life skills, a spirit of unity, and a strong ethical foundation. Through disciplined inquiry, compassionate service, and unwavering integrity, we empower our students to emerge as leaders and changemakers—citizens committed to building a just, inclusive, and progressive society.

coatOfArms.mottoMeaning: Derived from the Holy Father's maxim 'Caritas vestra magis ac magis abundet in scientia'.
coatOfArms.history: Before its foundation on October 9, 1946, the college received its motto from His Holiness the Pope: 'Caritas in Scientia'. The seal features Saint Philomena, a Greek princess and virgin martyr discovered in May 1802 at the Catacombs of Priscilla.

bishops.name: Most Rev. Dr. Rene Feuga
bishops.title: MOST REV. DR. RENE FEUGA – FOUNDER PATRON (1946-1964)
bishops.description: Bishop René-Jean-Baptiste-Germain Feuga, M.E.P., fondly known as Bishop Feuga, was the first Bishop of the Diocese of Mysore and founder Patron of St. Philomena's College. Consecrated in 1941, he vacated his episcopal mansion to start the first classrooms on October 9, 1946. Together with Maharaja Sri Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar's generous 29-acre land grant and blessings from Pope Pius XII, he laid the foundations of premier higher education in the Mysore region.
fullBiography: Bishop René-Jean-Baptiste-Germain Feuga, M.E.P., fondly known as Bishop Feuga was the first Bishop of the bifurcated Diocese of Mysore with its headquarters in Mysore and the founder Patron of St. Philomena's College. He was consecrated Bishop in 1941 and continued as the first prelate of the present Mysore diocese till he retired in 1962. His term was extended as Bishop till his demise in 1964.

Missions Etrangeres de Paris (MEP) commonly known as Paris Foreign Mission Society started sending priests to India in the latter part of the 18th century. The Vicariate of Mysore paved the way for the creation of the Diocese of Mysore in 1886. Rev. Fr. Rene Feuga came to India in 1913, chaired the French Department at St. Joseph's College Bangalore, and later chaired the French Department in Maharaja's College Mysore.

In 1929 he was appointed preceptor to Chamarajendra Wodeyar who succeeded as the Maharaja of Mysore in 1940. Bishop Feuga vacated his newly constructed Bishop's Mansion to house the initial classrooms of St. Philomena's College, while the Maharaja matched his sacrifice with 29 acres of land. He obtained the papal maxim 'Caritas in Scientia' from Pope Pius XII and equipped the first science labs.

bishops.name: Most Rev. Dr. Mathias Fernandes
bishops.title: Most Rev. Dr. Mathias Fernandes (1964-1985)
bishops.description: Bishop Mathias Sebastião Francisco Fernandes was appointed the second Bishop of Mysore in 1964. He spearheaded monumental infrastructural growth, constructing the college auditorium in 1966 and the ground floor of the library block in 1981. It was during his tenure as Patron that the College celebrated its historic Silver Jubilee.
fullBiography: Bishop Mathias Sebastião Francisco Fernandes commonly known as Bishop Mathias Fernandes was appointed the second Bishop of the present Diocese of Mysore and consecrated on February 3, 1964 at the young age of 46. Hailing from Goa, he chose to be a missionary in the large undivided diocese of Mysore.

His relentless work, mostly in rural areas like Shettihalli and Nagavalli, prompted him to uplift the poor through education, enabling hundreds of young people from rural areas to pursue higher studies and become lecturers, teachers, doctors and engineers.

Bishop Mathias Fernandes took keen interest in the growth of St. Philomena's College and was nominated twice to the Senate of the University of Mysore. In 1966 a much-needed elegant auditorium was constructed and in 1981 the ground floor of the library block, alongside the Silver Jubilee celebrations.

bishops.name: Most Rev. Dr. Francis Michaelappa
bishops.title: Most Rev. Dr. Francis Michaelappa (1987-1995)
bishops.description: Rt. Rev. Dr. Francis Michaelappa was consecrated the third Bishop of Mysore in 1987. Holding a Master's Degree in Communication and Journalism from Marquette University, USA, and profound scholarship in Kannada literature and Vachanas, he guided St. Philomena's College through pivotal academic consolidations.
fullBiography: Rt. Rev. Dr. Francis Michaelappa, a priest of the Arch-diocese of Bangalore, hailing from Harobale was consecrated the third Bishop of Mysore on May 27, 1987.

Besides studies in Philosophy and Theology, Bishop Michaelappa had a Master's Degree in Communication and Journalism from Marquette University, Milwaukee, Wisconsin, USA. He had vast knowledge of Kannada literature and quoted eloquently from the Vachanas in his speeches.

Simple and humble, but extraordinarily human, Bishop Michaelappa was proud to be chairman of St. Philomena's College, bravely managing the diocese and its institutions until his demise on March 17, 1993.

bishops.name: Most Rev. Dr. Joseph Roy
bishops.title: Most Rev. Dr. Joseph Roy (1995-2003)
bishops.description: Rt. Rev. Dr. Joseph Roy, born and brought up in Mysore, was the fourth Bishop and first local Bishop of Mysore. He oversaw the Golden Jubilee celebrations, the construction of the Octagonal Chapel in memory of Bishop Feuga, campus perimeter wall, library expansion, and new science laboratories.
fullBiography: Rt. Rev. Dr. Joseph Roy, born and brought up in Mysore, was the fourth Bishop of Mysore and the first local Bishop. He cherished having stayed during his minor seminary days in the present Administrative Block before it was handed over to the College.

Aware of the need to ensure academic growth, he supported Principal Rev. Fr. Leslie Moras in starting new courses and developing infrastructure, including the massive granite compound wall, three floors of the library block, and modern Computer Science, Microbiology, Biochemistry and Biotechnology laboratories.
The grand Golden Jubilee was celebrated under Bishop Roy's leadership, marked by the construction of the beautiful Octagonal Chapel at the college entrance in honour of Founder Bishop Rene Feuga.

bishops.name: Most Rev. Dr. Thomas Anthony Vazhapilly
bishops.title: Most Rev. Dr. Thomas Anthony Vazhapilly (2003-2017)
bishops.description: Under Bishop Thomas Anthony Vazhapilly, St. Philomena's College reached historic pinnacles: Autonomous status (2011), NAAC 'A+' grade (3.58 CGPA), College of Excellence (2015), 5-storey PG block, 1500-seat multi-purpose Indoor Stadium, and Diamond Jubilee with President Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.
fullBiography: Rt. Rev. Dr. Thomas Anthony Vazhapilly, the fifth Bishop of Mysore, held doctoral studies in Moral Theology from Gregorian University, Rome, and served as Professor and President of St. Peter's Pontifical Institute Bangalore before his election as Bishop on March 25, 2003.

Thanks to his collaboration with Principal Rev. Fr. Leslie Moras, PG courses were started in 2008 with a massive 5-storey PG block housing 14 programmes, a research centre, a 5-storey ladies' hostel for 350 students, and an international student body from 33 countries and 19 Indian states.

Under his chairmanship, the college achieved Autonomous status in 2011, NAAC A+ accreditation (3.58 CGPA), College with Potential for Excellence (2010), College of Excellence (2015), the 1500-seat Indoor Stadium, and Diamond Jubilee celebration inaugurated by President Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam.

rector.name: Rev. Dr. Lourdu Prasad Joseph
rector.title: Rector and Manager
rector.salutation: Preparing Global Citizens through Value-based Excellence
rector.quote: At Philomena’s, we do not merely educate — we inspire, transform, and empower. We nurture individuals who are intellectually competent, morally upright, and socially responsible — true global citizens ready to make a meaningful difference in the world.
text: At St. Philomena’s college (Autonomous), we stand on the proud shoulders of a rich and inspiring legacy that began on 9th of October 1946 — an era when education was envisioned not merely as a pathway for employment, but as a means of personal transformation and nation building. Founded through the farsighted vision of Rev. Dr. Rene Feuga and inaugurated by Sri Jayachamarajendra Wodeyar, the king of the then princely state of Mysore, the institution has evolved into one of the most respected centres of higher learning in the region.

From its very inception, the college has been guided by the profound motto “Caritas in Scientia” — Service expressed through the pursuit of knowledge. This guiding principle continues to define our academic philosophy, blending intellectual rigour with ethical grounding. Over the decades, the college has grown into a multidisciplinary academic hub offering a comprehensive range of undergraduate, post graduate, and research programmes. As an autonomous college, we enjoy the academic freedom to design innovative curricula that are responsive to contemporary global demands while rooted in human values.

A defining feature of our institution is its vibrant and diverse student community. With learners from different States across India and countries worldwide, the campus represents a true global village. This multicultural environment fosters inclusivity, cross-cultural understanding, and a broader worldview — qualities essential for leadership in a globalized society.

As we move forward, we remain steadfast in our vision to evolve into a globally recognized institution, with aspirations for attaining University status. We are committed to fostering innovation, expanding research capabilities, and strengthening industry-academia collaborations to meet the challenges and opportunities of the future. At Philomena’s, we do not merely educate — we inspire, transform, and empower. We nurture individuals who are intellectually competent, morally upright, and socially responsible — true global citizens ready to make a meaningful difference in the world. We warmly welcome students, parents, and stakeholders to be part of this enduring journey of excellence.

principal.name: Dr. Ravi J.D. Saldanha
principal.title: Principal
principal.salutation: Empowering Minds, Enriching Lives through Values and Excellence
principal.quote: May Philo’s 2025 not only showcase our achievements and aspirations, but also inspire us to dream bigger, seek truth with courage, and journey together in the spirit of Christian love and fellowship.
text: The academic year 2025–26 holds special significance for the Philo’s fraternity as we celebrate the Oak Jubilee, marking the 80th year of the establishment of our esteemed institution. This milestone is not merely a celebration of years, but a tribute to a rich legacy of excellence, service, and commitment to higher education.

A number of programmes and activities have been planned as part of the Jubilee celebrations, and this magazine offers a glimpse into many of these meaningful initiatives and achievements. The Jubilee invites each one of us to rediscover our roots, renew our commitment to quality education, and continue striving towards academic and human excellence. On this memorable occasion, we gratefully acknowledge the invaluable contribution of our Management, teachers — both past and present — students, non-teaching staff, alumni, and all those who, in visible and invisible ways, have contributed to the remarkable growth of this institution over the years.

As the Academic Head of the college, I remain deeply grateful to Rev. Dr. Lourdu Prasad Joseph, Rector of St. Philomena’s Educational Institutions, whose visionary leadership continues to nurture an environment rooted in the true spirit and charism of Philo’s. I also extend my sincere gratitude to Rev. Fr. Gnanapragasam, Campus Administrator, for his constant support and accompaniment; Rev. Fr. David Sagayraj, Assistant to the Rector, for his cooperation; the Academic Heads, Deans, Heads of Departments, teaching and non-teaching staff, and our beloved students, all of whom have been a constant source of strength throughout this academic year.

I place on record my appreciation to the Editorial Team, especially Dr. Yamuna B. Raj, for their dedication, creativity, and tireless efforts in bringing out this magazine with such thoughtfulness and care.
May Philo’s 2025 not only showcase our achievements and aspirations, but also inspire us to dream bigger, seek truth with courage, and journey together in the spirit of Christian love and fellowship.
